title: The only place experience happens
blurb: What the present moment is, why minds wander, and what the evidence says about mindfulness and awe.
description: Third film in a small series on time. It asks what the present actually is: a short window your brain assembles and attention steers. You meet the gorilla nobody sees, the cold-water experiment, the mind that wanders, and an honest account of what mindfulness and awe can do.
takeaways: Minds wander nearly half the time, and what matters most is whether the wandering is pleasant and interesting.
The experienced present is assembled by the brain, and attention decides a great deal about what makes it in.
Memory keeps the worst moment and the ending, so the remembering self and the experiencing self disagree.
Mindfulness programs show small to moderate benefits, and have not been shown to beat other active treatments.
Awe can make time feel more available, and a minute of really looking is a cheap way into the present.
